title: Dynamic Workflows in Claude Code
description:
Anthropic released dynamic workflows alongside Opus 4.8, and this is the feature that changes how Claude Code handles complex work.

Instead of one long-running agent trying to plan, execute, remember constraints, and verify itself inside one context window, Claude can now write a JavaScript workflow for the task. That workflow can spawn separate agents, assign focused jobs, use different worktrees, choose which model each sub-agent uses, and merge the result.

The important distinction is that normal subagents are usually one-off helpers. Dynamic workflows are the control system around them. Claude can decide the order of work, which agents verify other agents, when to loop, when to stop, and how to synthesize the output.

Use it for tasks that are long, messy, adversarial, or need independent checks: flaky tests, big refactors, claim verification, source-heavy research, ranking, tournaments, and session-mining for repeated mistakes.

Caveat: it uses more tokens, so it is not for every bug fix.
